blocks.text: Picsart shipped an MCP server. Most people read that as "another integration" and scrolled past.

Here is what it actually means. One line in your terminal, and an agent on your machine can generate video, images and audio across 201 models — and every one of those generations comes out of your credit balance, without a confirmation step.
Then I read the pricing page. There is a question in the FAQ: can I set a spending limit per run? The answer is no, not in the CLI today.
So I went through the whole surface - CLI, MCP, Skills, batch - to find where the actual brakes are. They exist. They are just not where you would expect, and nobody puts them in the announcement.
Here is the whole thing.
1. The numbers first
Read line seven against line one. The same catalogue is reachable five ways, and all five spend the same balance.
That is the part worth sitting with. Your agent, your cron job and your browser tab are three doors into one wallet.
2. Five doors, one account
The docs split it cleanly. The app is for exploring. MCP and Skills are for working inside an agent. The CLI is for scheduled and batch work. The SDK is for Node apps. REST is for everything else.
What makes this more than a feature list: the model ids are identical across all five. A model you find in the app runs in a shell script with the same string.
The CLI and the MCP server also share one credentials file and one balance. Authenticate once with gen-ai login and both are live.
There is no separate API key for the agent path. That is convenient, and it is exactly why the spending question matters.
3. The catalogue is the product, not any one model
201 models across 31 providers. Sora, Veo, Kling, Seedance, Flux, Nano Banana, Recraft, ElevenLabs, Topaz, Runway, Wan, Qwen.
New frontier models get added to the same endpoint. No migration on your side, no extra contract.
This is the same argument as the app, moved one layer down. A wide catalogue does not make anyone's work better by itself.
What it buys is routing. Picking a model becomes a parameter in a call instead of a procurement decision.
And routing only becomes useful when something can reason about which model fits. That something is now the agent sitting in your editor.
4. Thirteen tools, and seven of them are free
Connecting the server exposes thirteen tools. The split is the important part.
Nothing in the second block asks you first. The agent decides, the call lands, the credits go.
Which means the engineering problem here is not "can the agent generate". It is "does the agent check before it generates".
5. The four-call flow that keeps an agent honest
The docs recommend a chain, and the chain is the guardrail.
picsart_preflight is the piece to build around. One call returns { model, valid, errors?, credits } - the payload check and the price in the same response.
A wrong parameter surfaces as an error instead of a failed generation you already paid for.

Two caveats the docs state plainly. Some models do not expose per-call pricing and return null for credits. And a quote reflects the exact parameters you pass, so duration, resolution and count change it.
Put preflight in the system prompt as a rule, not a suggestion. "Never call generate without a preflight on the same payload" is one sentence and it is the whole cost control you get.
6. Batch is where the CLI beats the agent
For volume, the CLI wins, and it is not close.
A manifest is a flat YAML list. Each item carries its own model, prompt and parameters, and image, video and audio items can sit in the same file.
MCP has no manifest. An agent doing a catalogue job loops and calls picsart_generate once per item.
That is one charge per call, with no batch-level view of the total. For anything above a handful of assets, hand the job to the CLI and let the agent write the manifest.
7. What bites on the first real run
Four behaviours, all documented, none of them obvious from the prompt box.
There is no per-run spending cap. A manifest runs until it completes or the balance empties.
If credits run out mid-batch, completed generations are not reversed. You top up and resume the same run id.
Resume re-runs only the failures. Re-running the whole manifest instead pays a second time for everything that already worked.

And no tool anywhere in the MCP contract accepts a filesystem path. Every image and video input is a URL, which is why picsart_drive upload exists - it hands back a CDN url you can pass straight into the next call.
8. Skills are the knowledge layer, the CLI is the engine
A skill is not a second API. It is a bundle that teaches an agent what Picsart can do and which command to run.
The flagship bundle is gen-ai-use, and it covers the full catalogue. The same bundle works across Claude Code, Cursor and Windsurf - only the install path differs.
One detail people miss: skills call the CLI underneath, so gen-ai login is still required no matter how the skill was installed.
The practical effect is that model choice stops being your job. You describe the outcome, the agent picks the model and builds the parameters.
That is also the risk. An agent choosing a video model is an agent choosing a price.
9. Media Studio is a separate connector, and it does the opposite job
The MCP server creates media from a description. Media Studio assembles media out of material you already have.
Joining clips with transitions, captions over footage, transcribing speech, reframing a wide video for a phone, title cards from templates.
Two things the docs warn about, and both would have cost me a render. Ask which fonts are available before asking for styled text, because a font outside its list comes out blank.
And nothing is saved while you work. The piece lives in the conversation until it renders, so building across three chats loses it.
Preview thumbnails are free. Checking before a render is the cheapest habit in the whole stack.
10. Where I would not use this
Single assets. Opening the app is faster than describing a generation to an agent that then describes it to a model.
Anything where you cannot name the model you want. A wide catalogue with no opinion behind it produces a lot of plausible, wrong output.
And unattended loops on an account with a large balance, until you have watched one real batch finish and know what the total looks like.
The point
The interesting shift is not that Picsart added AI models. It is that a creative platform now behaves like infrastructure - an endpoint, a credit meter, a dry-run call, a resume command.
The tools that spend money are the loud ones. The tools that decide whether money gets spent are free, and they are the ones worth wiring into your prompts.
Preflight before generate. Manifest before agent loop. Preview before render.
Three rules, and the whole stack stops being a gamble.

Figures are recreations built from Picsart's published developer documentation as of September 2026, not live screenshots. Model and tool counts move weekly, so check the current numbers before quoting them.
If you want more breakdowns like this, I post one every couple of days on X and Telegram.
My Picsart setup, the same one behind this walkthrough:
https://picsart.go.link/cE1qI

data.markdown:
```plaintext
1  picsart_model_catalog   pick a model              free
2  picsart_model_params    learn its exact inputs    free
3  picsart_preflight       validate and quote        free
4  picsart_generate        run it                    charges
```

```plaintext
gen-ai batch run manifest.yaml     runs a list of generations in parallel
gen-ai batch status <run-id>       progress
gen-ai batch resume <run-id>       re-runs only the failed jobs
--input-dir ./stills/              same operation over a whole folder
--script                           clean JSON, pipes into jq
--save-to-drive                    results land in your library, not ./output
```

```json
{ "name": "picsart_preflight",
  "arguments": {
    "model": "veo-3.1",
    "params": { "prompt": "a drone shot over a snowy ridge",
                "duration": 8, "resolution": "1080p" } } }
```

```plaintext
claude plugin marketplace add PicsArt/gen-ai-skills
/plugin install picsart@picsart
npx skills add PicsArt/gen-ai-skills     works for Codex too
```

```plaintext
free, call as often as needed
  picsart_model_catalog    the full catalogue as data
  picsart_model_params     parameter schema for one model
  picsart_preflight        validates a payload and quotes its cost
  picsart_credits          balance and quota
  picsart_job_status       polls an async job
  picsart_list_models      visual picker widget
  picsart_drive            list, upload, move, delete

spends credits
  picsart_generate         any model, image, video, audio, text
  picsart_remove_bg        background removal
  picsart_change_bg        background replacement from a prompt
  picsart_enhance          upscale
  picsart_vectorize        raster to SVG
```

```plaintext
models in the catalogue              201
providers behind them                31
CLI and MCP general availability     28 April 2026
tools exposed over MCP               13
tools that cannot spend credits      7
tools that spend credits             6
interfaces onto the same account     5   app, MCP, CLI, SDK, REST
cost of a pricing quote              0   free dry run, no model invoked
per-run spending limit in the CLI    none today
```
